correctness.rationale: Exact held-input solution gives X_{j+1}=((k+1)e^{-H_j}-k)X_j. IID moments yield E[X_j^2]=X_0^2 V^j with V a closed quadratic. Deterministic Schur boundary hcrit=log((k+1)/(k-1)), exact boundary identity V-1=2(k-1)(c-1)((k-1)c-1) supplies strict rescue for 1<k<2. For k>=2, V<1 implies u^2+v^2<2 and hence (k+1)^2e^{-2h}=AB>(k-1)^2, contradiction at h>=hcrit. Exact witness has stochastic V=38567/40000 and periodic 1681/1600. Standalone SymPy checks and 42,000 rational samples passed, but quantified validity rests on these fully written analytic arguments.

originality.rationale: The precise conjunction is a necessity-and-sufficiency gain-two cutoff for mean-square rescue of periodically unstable scalar zero-order-hold feedback by iid equiprobable symmetric positive intervals of the same mean. Full-text 2013 Markov/LMI and robust sampled-data works do not state this exact quantifier or cutoff; the 2022 mixed-interval enhancement and 2023 stochastic-sampling papers available at abstract level describe related phenomena but not this exact cutoff. Repeated semantic searches of published research records retrieved different sampled/control claims. Priority remains qualified because plausible 2022/2023 complete texts and parts of the older scalar switching literature could not be reviewed.
residual_risks: The complete 2022 Jin–Wang–Wang article is a plausible priority source; full text unavailable after OA/arXiv and institutional access attempts.
The 2023 Wang–Zhu complete article and 2012 Tang–Zeng–He–Zhang mathematical text were not fully accessible; no unsupported full-document noncoverage claim is made.

Specialized scalar iid switching and stochastic sampled-data results may contain an equivalent gain-two threshold under different notation; semantic searches and accessible full literature cannot conclusively exclude this.

value.rationale: The motivating control-design gap is whether randomizing update times without changing mean spacing can recover a periodically unstable fixed-gain loop. The theorem completely answers that natural yes/no question in a canonical scalar zero-order-hold model with a sharp and non-obvious gain=2 boundary and supplies an exact, reproducible strict counterexample to the inference that periodic instability at the mean interval forbids mean-square stabilization. The no-go half gives a meaningful design restriction and rules out all binary symmetric timing amplitudes in the high-gain regime; neither proof nor application requires a more general extension. It does not claim novel general mixed-period stabilization, arbitrary jitter laws or time-normalized performance.
